primitives.name: ELO calibration as a winner predictor
primitives.verbatim_quote: Calibration reference for OUR model probs — verified: against WIN outcomes (their intended target) 538 ELO is excellently calibrated (Brier 0.2203, n=1,536; every decile observed ≈ predicted within ±3pp).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'ELO': "FiveThirtyEight's Elo rating system", 'win': 'Binary win outcome (1 if home team wins, 0 otherwise)', 'elo_prob1': 'Elo-based probability estimate for home team win', 'Brier': 'Mean squared error between predictions and outcomes'}
primitives.assumptions: Games are independent, no hidden variables affecting both Elo and outcomes, sufficient data coverage across all rating ranges.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Poorly calibrated for binary cover outcomes (home team covers spread), but perfectly calibrated for binary win outcomes.

layer2.mapping: Elo calibration maps directly to GSI conformal prediction intervals for win probabilities, enabling probabilistic winner bets with verified risk.
layer2.telemetry: Observed win calibration Brier score (lower is better) relative to -110 betting lines.

primitives.name: ELO is useless for covers
primitives.verbatim_quote: Against the market's closing number it has no value — it would have lost ~4% per bet flat betting its picks at -110.
primitives.assumptions: Market is efficient, no mispricing, and Elo is a complete summary statistic of public information.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Complete loss of predictive edge when used as a cover-prediction tool against closing spreads.

layer2.mapping: The derived kernel is the "market-adjusted Elo" residual, which captures what the closing spread adds beyond Elo's public-information signal.
layer2.telemetry: Historical betting profit/loss (PnL) from using Elo picks versus closing spreads at standard odds (-110).

primitives.name: ELO trajectory as a feature
primitives.verbatim_quote: Elo trajectory as a FEATURE (not a price-beater): team-strength priors.
primitives.assumptions: Team strength is persistent and mean-reverting, and Elo captures this efficiently without overfitting.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Effective as a static feature in models that combine it with other signals, but fails as a standalone price-beating forecast.

layer2.mapping: The Elo trajectory maps to a state-transition kernel in GSE, representing temporal evolution of team strength for situational reasoning.
layer2.telemetry: Contribution of Elo features to downstream model performance (e.g., explained variance in cover margins).

primitives.name: ELO no edge against closes
primitives.verbatim_quote: This is consistent with everything else we've found: public engines do not beat closes.
primitives.assumptions: Public engines incorporate all publicly available information, leaving no exploitable inefficiency.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Edge collapses to zero when tested against the final, fully-quoted closing spread.

layer2.mapping: The derived kernel is the "public-engine-minus-close" residual, which should be white noise if markets are efficient.
layer2.telemetry: Statistical significance of any remaining predictive skill after accounting for closing spreads.

reasoning_traces.think:
FiveThirtyEight's NFL Elo is a pinnacle of public, transparent statistical modeling designed specifically for predicting match winners. Its core strength lies in producing well-calibrated win probabilities, meaning its stated confidence levels accurately reflect long-run frequencies. However, this calibration is conditional on the win outcome, not on point-spread covers. When evaluated against closing spreads—a different, more complex target—Elo's performance degrades sharply. It underperforms even a naive 50/50 guess, yielding a Brier score worse than random guessing and a winning percentage below the break-even point for standard -110 betting odds. This failure mode arises because the closing spread already incorporates the exact information that Elo provides about team strength, plus additional adjustments for game context and public sentiment. Consequently, Elo offers no incremental predictive edge for betting on whether a team will cover the spread. Instead, it functions primarily as a high-quality, freely available dataset of game-level win probability estimates, serving as an excellent reference or feature input for building custom models. Its true value is as a calibrated prior for team strength, rather than as a direct price-beating signal.
